name: continuous-improvement

metadata.title: Continuous Improvement & Learning
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Analyze process execution log and implement improvements for future iterations. Use at the end of every process to learn from execution and improve templates/steps.

prerequisites: Process execution log (log.json) with user interactions
specificActions: Read Process Log: Load log.json; parse all user interactions and change requests; identify patterns and recurring issues; note high iteration counts
Analyze for Improvements: Group similar user corrections; identify corrections that could be automated; find missing validations; detect documentation gaps
Prioritize Improvements: Rank by frequency, impact, and ease; focus on high frequency + high impact + easy to implement; limit to top 3-5
For Each Improvement: Propose to user (What, Why, Impact, Scope); investigate solution; IMPLEMENT ACTUAL CHANGES to files; request approval; document improvement
CRITICAL: Improvements must be IMPLEMENTED, not just documented. This means actually modifying template files, step files, or guidance documents to prevent recurrence.
MANDATORY: Propose ALL improvements before completing; user must approve/reject each
Summarize All Improvements: List improvements made (with file paths modified) and skipped; provide recommendations
tools: read_file - Read log.json and target files
bestPractices: Propose all improvements: Before completing, ensure ALL identified improvements have been proposed
One at a time: Only implement one improvement at a time
Always get approval: User must approve before proceeding
Atomic changes: Keep each improvement focused and self-contained
No traceback: Don't reference the previous state in the improved version
Clean implementation: Make it look like it was always there
IMPLEMENT, don't just document: Every approved improvement must result in actual file modifications (templates, steps, docs) - documentation alone is NOT an improvement
Show the diff: After implementing, show what files were modified and what changed
DEEP DIVE REQUIRED: Never propose a shallow fix - always trace actual execution and identify ALL affected files across the framework
VERIFY BEFORE PROPOSING: Confirm the target files were actually used in this process before proposing changes to them

substeps.name: Init-Step: Confirm Principles
substeps.description: Recall operating principles before starting this step
actions: Read `.processes/steps/_components/operating-principles.md` and recall all principles
Output: '✓ Principles confirmed for this step'

substeps.name: Read Process Log (Comprehensive Analysis)
substeps.description: Load and comprehensively parse ALL sections of the process execution log
actions: Load process log from .user-processes/active/{process-name}/log.json
COMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS - Analyze ALL of the following log sections:
- steps[].userInteractions: Every user interaction, request, correction, and feedback
- steps[].problemsEncountered: Issues that occurred during each step
- steps[].decisionsMade: Choices the agent made that could be questioned or improved
- steps[].agentReasoning: Logic behind actions (may reveal flawed assumptions)
- steps[].actionsTaken: Full action history (may reveal inefficiencies)
- steps[].filesModified: File modification patterns and iteration counts
PRIORITY EXTRACTION - Identify and prioritize flagged entries:
- Find ALL userInteractions where forImprovementStep: true - these are explicitly flagged for review
- Extract ALL potentialImprovement values - these are user-provided improvement suggestions
- Create a priority list of flagged items to analyze first
PROCESS-WIDE OBSERVATIONS - Review aggregated insights:
- processWideObservations.patternsDetected: Cross-step patterns already identified
- processWideObservations.userFeedbackSummary: Aggregated user feedback
- processWideObservations.recommendationsForFuture: Prior recommendations to action
- processWideObservations.efficiencyMetrics: Performance data for trend analysis

substeps.name: Analyze for Improvements (with Deep Dive)
substeps.description: Identify improvement opportunities from the log with thorough root cause analysis - do NOT propose shallow fixes
actions: ANALYZE FLAGGED ITEMS FIRST: Start with entries from priority list (forImprovementStep: true and potentialImprovement values)
SECTION-SPECIFIC ANALYSIS:
- From problemsEncountered: Identify recurring problems, systemic issues, preventable errors
- From decisionsMade: Question choices, identify alternatives, spot questionable patterns
- From agentReasoning: Find flawed logic, incorrect assumptions, misunderstandings
- From actionsTaken: Spot inefficiencies, redundant actions, unnecessary steps
- From userInteractions: Group corrections, identify repeated manual interventions
- From filesModified: Note high iteration counts, identify files needing frequent rework
- From processWideObservations: Review pre-aggregated patterns and recommendations
Group similar user corrections
Identify steps with multiple iterations
Find documentation gaps
Detect repeated manual interventions
TRACE ACTUAL EXECUTION: Review log.json to identify exactly which files were used during this process (which prompts, which steps, which templates)
IDENTIFY ALL AFFECTED FILES: For each improvement, find ALL files in the framework that could be affected - not just one obvious file
CHECK FRAMEWORK-WIDE IMPACT: Consider if the issue exists in multiple places (e.g., both process-new.md AND process-continue.md)
VERIFY FILE USAGE: Before proposing a fix to any file, confirm that file was actually relevant to this process execution
ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS: Ask 'why did this happen?' at least 3 times to find the true root cause, not just the symptom
DOCUMENT REASONING: For each improvement, document: (1) What files were actually used, (2) What files need changes, (3) Why each file needs changes

substeps.name: Prioritize Improvements
substeps.description: Rank improvements by frequency, impact, and ease
actions: Score each improvement by: Frequency, Impact, Ease
Focus on high frequency + high impact + easy to implement
Limit to top 3-5 improvements

substeps.name: Implement Each Improvement (Iteratively)
substeps.description: For each prioritized improvement, propose, implement ACTUAL FILE CHANGES, and get approval
actions: a. Propose Improvement: Present What, Why, Impact, Scope, Target Files to modify
b. Get User Approval: Wait for user to approve/reject the proposed improvement
c. Investigate Solution: Research approach, identify exact files and sections to modify
d. Implement Change: ACTUALLY MODIFY the target files (templates, steps, docs) using write/search_replace tools
e. Show Changes: Present what files were modified and the specific changes made
f. Document Improvement: Update memory with file paths modified and change summary
CRITICAL: Step (d) must result in actual file modifications - documenting the problem without changing files is NOT implementing an improvement

substeps.name: Mandatory: Propose ALL Improvements
substeps.description: Ensure all identified improvements are proposed to user
actions: Checklist:
- Have all identified improvements been proposed?
- Has the user approved/rejected each?
- Have all approved improvements been implemented?
- Have all rejected improvements been documented with reasons?

substeps.name: Summarize All Improvements
substeps.description: Create final summary of all improvements
actions: List all improvements made
List improvements skipped and why
Provide recommendations for future work

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: Do modified process files conform to type definitions? (Principle 7 - see `.processes/steps/_components/operating-principles.md`)
Output: '✓ Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Read log → Analyze for improvements (with deep dive: trace execution, find ALL affected files) → Prioritize → For each: propose → implement → approve → Next → Summarize all

fields: Improvements Implemented: Each with Change, Files Modified, User Approval, Impact

All identified improvements have been either implemented or deferred
User has approved all implemented changes
